_comment: Every ingredient of a baseline run that is not the stock platform, declared once.
This file exists because the same class of mistake happened three times: a
campaign was launched with an ingredient missing, and nothing noticed until
the verdicts were already wrong. gf180 lost its PDN and tapcell overrides and
would have graded every design dirty (10685 violations instead of 3); nangate45
lost its patched DRC deck, which the pilot had applied by hand so it lived in no
script; and a manually launched sign-off inherited the 2h default bound instead
of the intended 6h, costing 88 verdicts. Reviewing what was written cannot catch
an omission -- only a declared list, checked before the run, can.
The three layers are the attribution contract:
checking  = the grader. Official where possible; a modified checker needs an
equivalence argument, recorded here, or its verdicts mean nothing.
apparatus = not official, but applied IDENTICALLY to both arms and declared.
repair    = applied by the repair arm only. This is the measured credit.
Paths are relative to $D (the campaign root on the campaign host).

image.why: One pinned image for every run on every platform, so a toolchain change cannot be mistaken for a result.

ingredients.why: The stock FreePDK45 deck runs CONTACT.3 flat over the whole die and does not finish inside any usable bound; 36 workers sat on 167 designs for 11 hours. Tiling the LOCAL geometry rules took the same 167 designs to 11 minutes.
ingredients.equivalence: Antenna and the net-tracing rules stay in deep mode, because tiling a net-tracing check makes it WRONG rather than merely faster. Same-layout A/B on C00006: stock timed out at 7278s, patched reported its violations in 310s. The pilot ran this deck too, so both rounds are graded by the same ruler.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: The campaign must stop. Without it nangate45 sign-off does not complete, and a timeout is not a pass.
ingredients.enforced_by: experiments/signoff45.py resolve_deck(): defaults to this deck and REFUSES to run if it is missing or if R2G_DRC_DECK_OVERRIDE names a missing file. Before 2026-10-21 a hand launch without the env var silently graded with the stock deck.

ingredients.why: The stock gf180 PDN config emits Via2/Via3 with -split_cuts, which merge into 0.772x1.028 rectangles and violate GF's V2.1/V3.1 'every Via2/Via3 edge exactly 0.26 um'. Differs from the stock config by exactly one dropped clause.
ingredients.equivalence: Measured on audio_playout with the same deck and the same switches, only the overrides differing: 3 violations with it, 10685 without (V2.1 3480 + V3.1 3480 + DF.13_MV 1862 + DF.14_MV 1859). The pilot used it, so this is parity with the pilot, not an advantage over it.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: The campaign must stop. Every gf180 design would grade dirty and dual-clean would read ~0 against the pilot's 754.

ingredients.why: gf180 ships -distance 100 while its own DF.13/DF.14_MV rules cap the distance to the nearest substrate tap at 15 um. -distance 30 satisfies the rule.
ingredients.equivalence: Part of the same audio_playout measurement above (DF.13_MV and DF.14_MV account for 3721 of the 10685).
ingredients.fail_if_missing: The campaign must stop, for the same reason as the PDN config.

ingredients.why: The stock nangate45 tech LEF ships NO per-layer antenna rule at all (its .r2g-pre-antenna.orig backup has zero ANTENNAAREARATIO lines), so OpenROAD's repair_antennas has nothing to fire on while the sign-off deck grades antennas at 300:1. The installer adds ANTENNAMODEL OXIDE1 + ANTENNAAREARATIO 300 on all 10 routing layers.
ingredients.equivalence: Ratio 300 deliberately MATCHES the grader rather than relaxing it. Present in the toolchain since 2026-07-22, so the pilot and this round both ran with it.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: Not fatal, but the arms stop being comparable to the pilot and the antenna repair has no model to act on.

ingredients.why: ANTENNA_X1, the platform's only diode, ships ANTENNADIFFAREA 0.0, which OpenROAD rejects with GRT-0246 'No diode found'. The installer gives it a non-zero area so repair_antennas will accept it.
ingredients.equivalence: Same installer and same vintage as the antenna model, so both rounds have it.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: Not fatal, but no diode can be inserted, so the antenna repair cannot work at all.

ingredients.why: The frozen per-design period, utilization and die. Frozen rather than derived at run time, because a repair that cuts cell count would otherwise shrink its own die and move the goalposts.
ingredients.equivalence: One generator is the single place the die is computed; both arms read the same table files.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: The campaign must stop. A run without the frozen table is not the frozen baseline.
history: 2026-10-21: regenerated with the pin floor, core = max(area, pins/(4k), pdn). Moves nangate45 8 / sky130hd 10 / gf180 1 designs; none had read dual-clean. The nangate45 baseline ran on the previous tables (spec_pre_pinfloor_20261020_2109/), and exactly one dev design moves under the new ones -- C02939__multi_kernel_relu, which had failed with PPL-0024 -- so it alone is re-run. sky130hd and gf180 run on the new tables from the start.

2026-10-21 13:25: pin counts also taken from PPL-0024 logs (the pilot's, then the frozen re-run's) for designs that never wrote a DEF -- the very designs the floor is for. Moves nangate45 +47 / sky130hd +29 / gf180 +3; in nangate45 dev 24 more, none previously passing. All 25 dev PPL-0024 failures are now pin_floored and are re-run.

2026-10-21 15:12: nangate45 only. (1) Per-design die correction from each design's own PPL-0024 refusal in the pin-floor re-run (positions/perimeter measured 1.666-1.783 over 68 logs vs the derived 1.80): exactly the 6 designs still 0.2-0.6% short move, no other field of any existing entry changes. (2) 13 NEW entries sized from the repair arm's own synthesis (size_source=repair_arm_synth_stat) for designs the baseline cannot synthesise at all, so a repair-arm win is judged under the same period/die formula as its peers.

2026-10-21 18:50: hierarchical synth_stat reports were sized from their FIRST section (a submodule). Now the top's own section. nangate45 dev: exactly the 2 jsilicon designs change (area x1.47, x1.87; die 50->60, 50->67; period 1.0->1.6) -- both had failed placement at 111% utilization. Two held-out entries change too (one from a 36 um die to 174 um).

2026-10-22: sky130hd regenerated BEFORE its baseline with the hierarchical fix (size from the top module's synth_stat section) and --extra-pin-log-root rerun_nangate45_20261018/runs (the source of its 10 rerun_ppl_log pin counts -- omitting it zeroed them and un-floored C01139). Exactly 4 entries move, all top-module resizes: C00114/C00195 jsilicon, C01922 tang-nano rng, C02133 zirh (period 1.8 -> 16.0). Old table kept as spec_sky130hd.pre_topsize_20261022.json.

2026-10-22 (later): sky130hd IO_POS_PER_UM 1.087 -> 0.90, MEASURED from 28 PPL-0024 messages (positions / core perimeter 0.912-0.923); the derived value let the smoke run's pin-floored C01139 fail PPL-0024 again. Also reads the smoke run's PPL logs (--extra-pin-log-root rerun_sky130hd_smoke130_1022/runs). Exactly 49 entries move and every one is a pin-floored die (39 already floored grow, 10 newly floored); 0 other entries change. Previous table kept as spec_sky130hd.pre_k090_20261022.json.

2026-10-22 06:00: sky130hd port-buffer term. buffer_ports puts a clkdlybuf4s50_1 (3.68 x 2.72 = 10.0096 um2, platform LEF) on every IO port, which the area allowance (one multiplier on cell area) does not model: the running baseline's C00148 writeback_mux (1010 um2, 133 pins) got 131 of them and failed GPL-0301 at 104%, C00220 at 113%. Area term is now max(area x allowance, area + pins x 10.0096). Reproducibility checked first: with the term off the generator rebuilds the previous table byte-identically (54147ad1). Exactly 347 entries move (185 dev), only die/core (+1..+25 um, median +6) and the derived pdn_floored/pin_floored flags; no period changes. Baseline paused at 141/1249 designs; the 30 finished runs whose die moved were set aside (rerun_sky130hd_20261022/superseded_pre_portbuf/) and re-run. nangate45 unchanged (no GPL-0301 in its baseline); gf180 to be measured before its baseline. Previous table kept as spec_sky130hd.pre_portbuf_20261022.json.

ingredients.why: Six hours per design for the flow and for sign-off. The pilot used 7200 for sign-off, so a verdict earned only by the longer bound is ours and not like-for-like with the pilot -- which is why it is declared here rather than left implicit.
ingredients.equivalence: Applied to both arms. A design that still times out is NOT clean; no verdict is not a pass.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: A shorter bound silently costs verdicts: 88 nangate45 designs lost one to the 7200 default.
ingredients.enforced_by: signoff45.py passes DRC_TIMEOUT=--timeout and LVS_TIMEOUT=max(run_lvs.sh size table, --timeout) into the container, with the outer subprocess bound 900s above, and classifies the checker's own 'timed out after' as timeout. Before 2026-10-21 --timeout was the outer bound only and the inner DRC bound stayed at run_drc.sh's 7200 default. sky130hd/gf180: signoff_pass.py passes DRC_TIMEOUT=--timeout (outer +900); lvs130.py passes NETGEN_TIMEOUT and R2G_POWERED_NETLIST_TIMEOUT=--timeout with the outer bound --timeout+900 as the TOTAL (below reaper2.sh's 390-min age rule), and files an inner bound or a spent budget as timeout. Before 2026-10-22 lvs130.py passed no inner bound, so run_netgen_lvs.sh capped magic and netgen at its 3600 default.

ingredients.applies_to: ONLY designs diagnosed as antenna-only DRC violations with LVS already clean
ingredients.why: With both sides at ratio 300 the router reports 4 violating nets and the grader reports 208 on the same layout -- the models disagree inside the computation, not in their configuration. Over-constraining the router to 10:1 makes it repair until the grader's 300:1 is satisfied with margin. Validated on C00315: 208 antenna violations to 0, LVS still matching, worst slack 0.2748 -> 0.2754, at +11.9% instances and +3.4% cell area.
ingredients.not_gaming: This makes the ROUTER stricter than the rule, not the GRADER looser. The sign-off deck and its 300:1 are untouched and identical in both arms. It is the opposite direction from relaxing a rule, and it departs deliberately from install_nangate45_antenna.sh's choice of 300, whose stated intent was to match the grader.
rejected_alternatives: ANTENNACUMAREARATIO: no effect. The apparent 0->9 improvement came from a standalone check_antennas on a final DEF, an artificial setting; inside the flow the layout was byte-identical.
MAX_REPAIR_ANTENNAS_ITER_GRT/DRT = 10: no effect, byte-identical layout. The repair had already converged; it was never iteration-bound.
ratio 50: reduced violations on 5 of 5 designs and cleared none of them. Only zero counts toward dual-clean.
TECH_LEF in the design config.mk: silently overridden by the platform config's `=`. Any override must be a bind mount with a read-back assertion.

ingredients.why: Three defects of this driver's config generation, not of any RTL: (1) make splits paths on whitespace and has no quoting, so a source dir with a space became two nonexistent files (34 nangate45 dev designs never reached yosys); (2) a file both listed and `include`d by another listed file was read twice -> 'Re-definition of module' (15); (3) $readmem memory images (.hex/.mem/.init/.list...) listed as sources were parsed as HDL -> 'unexpected TOK_CONSTVAL' (9). Fixed by symlinking make-hostile paths through the work dir, dropping a listed file that another listed file includes ONLY when it defines a module and has no include guard, and dropping memory-image suffixes (a blacklist: a whitelist dropped a HardFloat `.vi` include from a passing design).
ingredients.equivalence: Regression gate over all 1249 dev designs: 58 configs change (34+15+9), all of them designs that failed; 0 passing designs change; 1191 byte-identical.
ingredients.fail_if_missing: The 58 designs fail before synthesis, in both arms.
